topics.headline: Eurozone and US inflation both poised to rebound in July
topics.summary: Deutsche Bank expects Euro Area HICP to rise to 3.0% from 2.8% (Spain's flash already confirming upward moves), while US CPI is broadly expected to rebound in July as energy prices stop falling — raising real odds both regions post higher YoY inflation next release, though the US print isn't due until August 12.

topics.headline: HY OAS at 2.77%, near cycle lows despite asymmetric widening risk
topics.summary: HY spreads sit at 2.77%, well off April's 4.61% tariff-driven spike, with recent moves tied to rate volatility rather than credit deterioration; strategists note spreads remain in the tightest 5% of 25-year readings, meaning statistically more room to widen than compress, but the Fed's hold and stable IG markets suggest no imminent stress catalyst over the next 30 days.

topics.headline: Bitcoin ETFs snap outflow streak, but inflows remain fragile
topics.summary: After four straight days of redemptions totaling $526M, US spot Bitcoin ETFs eked out a modest $32.1M inflow on July 29, led by IBIT, but analysts say this reflects easing selling pressure rather than renewed institutional conviction, especially with the White House digital asset report due and Bitcoin still stuck below the $65,000 breakout level.

topics.headline: VIX spikes to 20.66 on Fed hold, Iran tensions
topics.summary: VIX jumped 13% to 20.66 after a hawkish Fed hold and Iran-related Treasury sanctions, sitting well above its ~17 trailing-month average; history and crowded short-vol positioning suggest a real chance of further squeeze, though experts and mean-reversion patterns argue it likely fades back toward trend within 30 days.

topics.headline: Deal cadence stays hot: Constellation-hyperscaler 1.2GW PPA filed
topics.summary: Constellation's June 8-K dedicating 1.2GW of nuclear capacity to a hyperscaler, plus the Chevron-Microsoft Project Kilby deal and OpenAI-Oracle's 4.5GW Stargate expansion, show the 30-day announcement question resolving YES almost by default given continuous 2026 deal flow; the real uncertainty is deal quality, as critics note these commitments remain a fraction of hyperscalers' overall capex.
